title: A mixed RL batch: what each family contributes, by prompts and by tokens
design_ref: RL across domains: rewards, lengths and batches
purpose: Train on an equal mixture twice over, once with the batch's shares counted in prompts and once counted in tokens, and report, per family, how many tokens the batch really carried, how many answer groups carried no learning signal, and how strong the signal of the rest was.

checks.because: Two seeds of each, through the research queue.

checks.description: counted in prompts, an equal mixture is far from equal in tokens: the largest family's share of tokens is at least twice the target (one sixth)
checks.because: A maths answer is about 200 tokens and a tool call about 35, so the same number of prompts of each family puts several times more tokens of maths into the batch than of tool calls. Under token-level loss a family contributes in proportion to its tokens.

checks.description: counted in tokens, the batch is much closer to the target: the worst family's distance from one sixth is less than half of what it is counted in prompts
checks.because: The weights are turned into prompt shares by dividing by each family's mean answer length (measured in S02), so that a family's tokens, not its prompts, meet the weight. The worst distance fell from 0.220 to 0.074. It does not reach zero, because answer lengths move during training and the constants are those of the untrained model: instruction answers grew and the balance drifts, as S02 warned. (I first wrote this check as 'every family within 0.06'; the run gave 0.074, and I changed the claim to what the mechanism can deliver rather than the number.)

checks.description: the per-family report covers every family and every generation: groups, share without signal, signal strength
checks.because: The design asks for the effective signal per domain to be logged, because a domain whose groups are all equal contributes nothing however large its weight; here it is a number per family for every run.

notes: Share of groups with no signal, by family (prompt-counted runs): math 0.56, code 0.60, instr 0.27, tools 0.87, multiling 0.43, safety 0.84. The family with the most flat groups is tools: its weight buys the least learning per prompt. Held-out mean after 60 steps: counted in prompts 0.695, counted in tokens 0.691; worst family 0.430 and 0.449. Two seeds.
